sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: Alonso says he brought Caicedo back too early; doubtful for Leeds
briefs.summary: Moises Caicedo failed a late fitness test before Sunday's loss at Arsenal after lasting 14 minutes off the bench against Brighton, and Xabi Alonso said the problem is "not longer term" but admitted rushing him; the Evening Standard has him unlikely for Wednesday's Carabao Cup tie with Leeds and more likely for Hull on Saturday.

briefs.headline: De Zerbi faults his forwards and the medics' 60-minute limits
briefs.summary: After the scoreless draw at Forest, Roberto De Zerbi said his forwards must make "better decisions" and that he was "not happy" medical staff set 60-minute exits for Savio and Udogie; Sky's Paul Merson called airing it in public "worrying." Spurs are still without a league goal after three matches and host Everton Saturday at 12:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Stewart practices for the Bengals, and Golden says he 'looked good'
briefs.summary: Shemar Stewart, out all camp with a hyperextended left knee, practiced Monday; defensive coordinator Al Golden said "you saw him out there today, he looked good" and the team will check Tuesday for a setback. Zac Taylor said Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins "look good" after minor knocks. Tampa Bay visits Paycor Stadium Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Dodgers beat the Reds 6-3 on Hernandez's three-run homer
briefs.summary: Teoscar Hernandez's three-run homer in the sixth off Brandon Williamson decided Monday's series opener at Dodger Stadium; Ke'Bryan Hayes, back from the injured list, made two errors that set up two unearned runs, Cincinnati left 11 on base, and Chase Burns was held to three no-hit innings. Elly De La Cruz and Eugenio Suarez homered. The Reds are 69-75, fifth in the NL Central.

briefs.headline: Monken names rotating captains; Watson starts at Jacksonville
briefs.summary: Todd Monken will pick five captains each week and let players vote on permanent ones at season's end, saying "we have more leaders than five guys"; Week 1's are Deshaun Watson, Zion Johnson, Mason Graham, Tyson Campbell and Rex Sunahara. The Browns also signed tackle Zion Logue to the practice squad. Kickoff at EverBank Stadium is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Rested FC Cincinnati visits Philadelphia at 7:45 p.m. ET Wednesday
briefs.summary: The club's tune-in page sets Wednesday's kickoff at Subaru Park at 7:45 p.m. ET on Apple TV and FS1, settling the time question from Sunday's postponement notice. FC Cincinnati has four wins, a loss and a draw in midweek matches this year, the club says, and faces a Union side unbeaten since the summer break under interim coach Ryan Richter; no makeup date for the D.C. United match has been set.

briefs.headline: Gibson says 10 explosive plays a game 'is not good' after the Penn State shutout
briefs.summary: Tony Gibson called Saturday's shutout loss in State College "disappointing" and said the Herd "have too many good players" to manage 147 yards of offense; the defense gave up 10 explosive plays. Middle Tennessee, which beat Murray State in its opener, visits Joan C. Edwards Stadium Saturday at 7 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Hauser takes the first 35 minutes at Nebraska before it 'got out of hand'
briefs.summary: Ohio scored on its first three drives in Lincoln before Nebraska's Jamal Rule took over with 169 all-purpose yards and three touchdowns in his debut; John Hauser said he was proud of the start, Jack Fries made eight tackles and Ike Ackerman had two sacks. Jacksonville State visits Peden Stadium Saturday at 6 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Pirates outright Bethancourt on the off day before three at the White Sox
briefs.summary: Pittsburgh outrighted catcher Christian Bethancourt to the minors Monday after a weekend series win over the Angels; Bubba Chandler starts Tuesday's opener at Rate Field against Sean Burke at 7:40 p.m. ET. The Pirates are fourth in the NL Central, 5.5 out of a wild card.

briefs.headline: Rodriguez says lineman Darius Wiley is out for the season
briefs.summary: On his Monday radio show Rich Rodriguez said Wiley, carted off in Saturday's win over Coastal Carolina, has a severe ligament injury that "takes at least a year, maybe more," with surgery targeted by Friday; junior-college transfer Jeremiah Johnson steps in and Tobi Haastrup gets a bigger role. Tennessee-Martin visits Saturday at 1 p.m. ET.

sections.note: Hannan's Sept. 1 match at Roane County and Sept. 3 home match with Logan remain unreported by any outside source, and MaxPreps has now dropped both from the schedule, showing Roane at Ashton Sept. 24 and Logan away Oct. 13 with a 1-1 record; whether the two September fixtures were moved or never played is a question for the coach, and the paper prints no result. The Reds' and Pirates' records are from MLB's standings feed; the Premier League and MLS figures are Sky Sports' and FOX Sports' tables as read Tuesday morning.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu returns to the dohyo, calls the knee 'much better,' decides by Friday
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu practiced Tuesday at Tatsunami stable in Tokyo, offering his chest to lower-ranked wrestlers without a brace on his surgically repaired right knee: "It's gotten much better and there's strength in the leg." He took no bouts at Friday's Yokozuna Deliberation Council session, and swelling the next day forced a rest day. He will decide whether to enter the Aki basho (autumn tournament), which opens Sunday at Ryogoku Kokugikan, by the morning of Friday's bout-drawing meeting; he has missed two straight tournaments.

briefs.headline: Aonishiki takes his first bouts since July and calls the ankle 'not bad'
briefs.summary: Ozeki (champion) Aonishiki, the Nagoya winner, resumed full bout practice Tuesday at Ajigawa stable in Tokyo for the first time since the July tournament, taking roughly 15 to 20 bouts and saying "it wasn't bad"; he had skipped bouts on the August tour and at Friday's council session with a left ankle and toe problem. The same day a sponsor presented him a kesho-mawashi (ceremonial apron) in blue and yellow.

briefs.headline: Luzardo's 12-strikeout shutout lifts the Phillies past the Braves 1-0
briefs.summary: Jesus Luzardo threw the first complete game and shutout of his career Monday, two hits, one walk and 12 strikeouts in 109 pitches, and Kyle Schwarber's 43rd homer in the eighth was the only run at Citizens Bank Park. Atlanta's lead in the NL East is four games with 18 to play.

briefs.headline: Brewers beat the Cubs 4-3 on Chourio's two-run single and diving catch
briefs.summary: Milwaukee scored three in the eighth off Matthew Boyd Monday, Jackson Chourio's two-run single putting them ahead, and after Pete Crow-Armstrong homered in the ninth Chourio's diving catch ended it; Trevor Megill earned his 27th save. Chicago has lost two straight.

briefs.headline: Orioles beat the Guardians 6-4 as Cleveland and Toronto both lose
briefs.summary: Coby Mayo's first two-homer game carried Baltimore past Cleveland on Monday to snap a six-game skid, while the Athletics walked off Toronto on Jeff McNeil's infield single; the Guardians stay a game ahead of the Blue Jays for the last AL wild card.

briefs.headline: Qualifier Zheng beats Swiatek to reach the U.S. Open quarterfinals
briefs.summary: Zheng Qinwen took out No. 8 Iga Swiatek 7-5, 6-3 in Monday's fourth round after trailing by five games in the first set, the first qualifier to put Swiatek out of a major; Elena Rybakina won in straight sets against Naomi Osaka and Coco Gauff extended her winning streak to 10 matches. Alexander Zverev meets Botic van de Zandschulp, who came through a five-setter lasting 5 hours, 13 minutes, in the men's quarterfinals.

sections.note: Sumo copy was read on Yahoo Japan article pages carrying Kyodo, Jiji and Sports Hochi reports; the JSA's own pages showed no withdrawal notice Tuesday, and r/Sumo was unreachable for a 16th morning. Kirishima reportedly went 12-1 in 13 bouts with new sekiwake Fujinokawa at Otowayama on Monday, per Sponichi and Sanspo, but both originals were blocked and only an aggregator carried it, so the figure is not printed as fact. The Yokozuna Deliberation Council's joint training session was Friday, Sept. 4, at the Kokugikan, where Onosato took 15 bouts and chairman Hakkaku said his hips were still too high; the Aki basho opens Sunday, Sept. 13, and runs through Sept. 27. Monday was the U.S. Open's fourth round; Alcaraz-Shelton and Sabalenka-Noskova are Tuesday's quarterfinals. The Yankees, Mariners and Astros were idle Monday.

coming_in.item: The first of two youth waterfowl days is Saturday, Sept. 19, per the DNR's 2026-27 migratory bird summary; the bag is set by the summary's waterfowl footnote, and HIP registration is required.

prime.item: Limits page effective Sept. 2: an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one per day, and the division says possessing a red drum over 27 inches is unlawful; Coastal Angler's Sept. 1 column calls September a redfish month, with the fish on shrimp and baitfish.

Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 14 to 20 inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day; the division's Sept. 4 plan review says 2025's spring and fall indices showed higher abundance despite the cold stun.

Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, with one fish over 25 inches allowed; Coastal Angler has them at the bridges, docks and deepwater oyster rocks on cut shrimp.
Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 12-inch fork-length minimum and 15 per day; the Fisherman's Post September report has them on casting jigs from the surf and piers, best early in the morning.

going_out.item: Day eight of the two-week window, which closes at 11:59 p.m. Monday, Sept. 14, under proclamation FF-27-2026: one fish per day, 15-inch minimum, no harvest under a Recreational Commercial Gear License. A separate proclamation, FF-37-2026, opens the commercial pound-net season in the northern area Sept. 15.
The early Canada goose season closes Sunday, Sept. 13, per the DNR's 2026-27 migratory bird summary: five a day and 15 in possession, in aggregate, with HIP registration required.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

sections.note: The DNR's 2026-27 migratory bird summary opened with readable text for the first time Tuesday: it lists no September teal season in West Virginia; mourning dove runs Sept. 1-Oct. 11, Nov. 2-15 and Dec. 7-Jan. 10 at 15 a day; rails and snipe opened Sept. 1; ducks open Oct. 3 and woodcock Oct. 17; Stonewall Jackson WMA is newly under special dove regulations and South Branch WMA no longer is. North Carolina's September teal season, Sept. 10-19 east of U.S. 17, is the Wildlife Resources Commission's and is not a Marine Fisheries rule. Gauley season opens Friday, Sept. 11: the National Park Service's whitewater page, updated Aug. 26, lists Corps releases from Summersville Dam on Sept. 11-14, 18-21 and 25-28 and Oct. 2-5, 9-12 and 17-18, and Gauley Fest runs Sept. 17-20 at Nicholas County Veterans Memorial Park in Summersville (American Whitewater). The elk-tour date conflict is resolved: the wvdnr.gov page carrying Sept. 6 is last year's release, and the DNR's Aug. 28, 2026 release as carried by Lootpress and WVOW puts the first Chief Logan tour on Sunday, Sept. 13, with tours on weekends through Oct. 24. WVDNR's National Hunting and Fishing Day is Saturday, Sept. 19, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. at Stonewall Resort State Park, adults $10 and 14 and younger free. Marine Fisheries' Sept. 4 plan review says the southern flounder stock shows early signs of recovery and the northern red drum stock is not overfished, with concern about fishing mortality. Bluefish: the limits table says 5 a day, but the footnote caps private anglers at 3, with 5 only on for-hire trips. No trout stocking is posted on the DNR's stocking page.

waters.working: Down from Sunday morning's post-storm reading of 166 cfs and back to low, clear late-summer water. At 71 this is a long-leader, small-fly river: a size 16 caddis or a small stonefly nymph fished through the pocket water and plunge pools, with caddis, stoneflies and sculpin the forage, and a small streamer along the undercut banks first thing. NWS Charleston's 5:17 a.m. discussion has warm, placid weather through Wednesday afternoon, then a front bringing showers and storms Wednesday night into early Friday with heavy downpours and a localized flash-flood concern, so the window is today and Wednesday.
waters.note: USGS answered on the fourth try this morning after 503s from all three gauges at 5:32 a.m. The Forest Service's July 17 alert for FR 86, the Williams River Road, listed a closure from FR 216 to Route 150 through Aug. 31 and has not been updated; its Aug. 12 alert says the Tea Creek Campground bridge replacement began Aug. 28 with the bridge and campground open during the work.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.0 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Easing a few tenths a day since the weekend rise. Normal pool is structure fishing: shad are the forage, so a white swimbait or a spoon over the wing-dam tips at first light, then a football jig dragged into the slack behind the tips once the sun is on the water.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 26.3 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The Weather Service's forecast for the Huntington gauge, read at 5 a.m., has it easing to 25.9 feet by 8 a.m. with no flooding. A little current still runs on the lock wall and in the barge cuts: a crawfish-colored jig pitched into the slack behind the cuts, and a skipjack-pattern swimbait along the riprap where the flow pins bait against it. The Corps' Huntington District site was unreachable again, so no lock notice is printed.

waters.reading: Sound highs 6:10 AM at 3.7 ft and 6:48 PM at 4.6 ft at Hampstead; lows 12:37 AM at 0.6 ft and 12:33 PM at 0.1 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 6:10 AM and 6:48 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The Fisherman's Post September report, published Tuesday, Sept. 1 and a week old, has East Coast Sports on Spanish mackerel and bluefish on casting jigs from the surf and piers, best early, with a few tarpon and cobia on live bait at the pier ends and the fall king bite still to come; Coastal Angler's Sept. 1 column has black drum inside at the bridges, docks and deepwater oyster rocks on cut shrimp, speckled trout on the same drop-offs and potholes, and slot reds on gold spoons, topwater plugs and soft plastics as the shrimp move. Reds want the last of the fall, which runs into the 12:33 PM low; work the flood into the 6:48 PM high for trout on the grass edges. Waning crescent at 13%, so neap tides and a gentle inlet. Water 79.9F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. NWS Wilmington has a high rip current risk for Pender beaches from 6 a.m. through this evening with 2-to-4-foot surf, a northeast wind around 15 mph and a strong north-to-south longshore current, easing to moderate Wednesday; the National Hurricane Center's 2 a.m. outlook expects no tropical cyclone formation in the Atlantic over the next seven days.

kicker: The Aki basho opens Sunday in Tokyo, five days out, with Hoshoryu's entry decided Friday; the Pirates open at the White Sox at 7:40 p.m. ET and the Reds are at the Dodgers at 10:10.
